$comment: Lanes of the stability lab (plans/cmux-next/chrome-parity/p10-stability.md 3A; runner stability-lab.py). Tiers: fast lanes run on each new lab tip and decide its coverage; long lanes run on the newest tip; feed lanes run when the nightly-next feed has a new newest build and test that build, not a tip (subject feed). The runner fills {app}, {previous_app}, {job}, {out} and {host}, writes the step's combined stdout and stderr to the lane's stdout path, puts the run's crash reports and panic logs in {out}/crashes, and gives the run to `stability-lab.py signatures`. `stability-lab.py lanes --check` validates this file.

lab-mini-fast.pool: lab M6 minis cmux15-24 except cmux20 (the perf cron's bench host)
lab-mini-fast.note: The skew and restore lanes run one after another on one lab mini per tip (about 15 min); the update lane runs on the same mini when the nightly-next feed has a new newest build. They are preemptible: a foreground step on that mini stops them, and the next tick runs them again.

lanes.pass: exit 0: every (direction, case) row is works, re-exec or fix. The bundled CLI of this tip (N) runs against the daemon of the previous lab tip (N-1) and the reverse, so both skew directions are covered. Running from the .app bundle also covers the re-exec half that the Linux workflow cannot.
exit 0: every report.json row passes (n/a rows do not count) after the quit, update and crash relaunches

lanes.pass: exit 0: no FAIL row (PENDING rows do not count). The feed's second item updates to its newest with live terminals and an agent turn.
